outputs.L3:
A method and an exhaust treatment system are provided for treating an exhaust stream that contains nitrogen oxides. The exhaust stream may originate, for example, from an internal combustion engine or another combustion process and may include various compounds containing nitrogen, carbon, and hydrogen, as well as soot particles.

In the method, the exhaust stream is first subjected to an oxidation step. During this first oxidation, compounds present in the exhaust stream that contain nitrogen, carbon, or hydrogen are oxidized. This oxidation may convert at least a portion of nitrogen monoxide into nitrogen dioxide and may also oxidize hydrocarbons, carbon monoxide, or other oxidizable components contained in the exhaust gas.

After the first oxidation step, a ratio between the amount of nitrogen dioxide and the total amount of nitrogen oxides in the exhaust stream is determined. This ratio may be expressed as the proportion of nitrogen dioxide relative to the combined amount of nitrogen monoxide and nitrogen dioxide. The determined ratio provides information about the composition of the nitrogen oxides downstream of the oxidation stage and can be used to optimize subsequent treatment of the exhaust gas.

A first additive is then introduced into the exhaust stream. The supply of this additive is actively controlled on the basis of the determined ratio between nitrogen dioxide and total nitrogen oxides. In this way, the quantity of additive supplied can be adjusted to the actual composition of the exhaust stream, improving the efficiency of the following catalytic reduction process. The additive may be a reducing agent or a precursor of a reducing agent suitable for reducing nitrogen oxides.

The exhaust stream is subsequently passed through a catalytic particulate filter. In this filter, nitrogen oxides are reduced by means of a catalytic reaction, while soot particles contained in the exhaust stream are captured by the filter structure. The catalytic particulate filter therefore performs two functions: it promotes the reduction of nitrogen oxides and, at the same time, traps particulate matter. The soot particles collected in the filter may be oxidized, thereby regenerating the filter and maintaining its particulate removal efficiency.

By combining the first oxidation step, the determination of the nitrogen dioxide-to-nitrogen oxides ratio, the controlled supply of the additive, and the catalytic particulate filter, the method and system provide effective treatment of exhaust gas containing nitrogen oxides and soot particles. This coordinated control can improve nitrogen oxide conversion, support soot oxidation, and enhance overall exhaust aftertreatment performance.
outputs.L4:
The method and system relate to the treatment of exhaust gas containing nitrogen oxides, particularly exhaust gas produced by combustion engines such as diesel engines. In this process, the exhaust stream is first subjected to an oxidation step in which at least part of the nitrogen monoxide present in the exhaust gas is converted into nitrogen dioxide. This produces a mixture of nitrogen oxides having a defined ratio of nitrogen dioxide to total nitrogen oxides.

After this initial oxidation, the composition of the exhaust gas is monitored. In particular, the ratio of nitrogen dioxide to the total amount of nitrogen oxides is measured or otherwise determined. This value is used as an important control parameter because the efficiency of the subsequent catalytic reduction depends strongly on the relative proportions of nitrogen dioxide and nitrogen monoxide in the exhaust stream.

Based on the measured ratio, an additive is introduced into the exhaust gas in a controlled manner. The additive may be a reducing agent or a precursor of a reducing agent, such as ammonia or a substance capable of releasing ammonia, for example a urea-water solution. The quantity of additive injected is adjusted so that the nitrogen oxides can be reduced as effectively as possible in a downstream catalytic stage.

The treated exhaust gas is then passed through a particulate filter provided with a catalytic coating. This coated particulate filter performs two functions at the same time. First, it acts as a filter that traps particulate matter, especially soot particles contained in the exhaust gas. Second, because of its catalytic coating, it promotes the reduction of nitrogen oxides using the injected additive. As a result, nitrogen oxides are converted into harmless components such as nitrogen and water.

In addition, the presence of nitrogen dioxide in the exhaust gas supports the oxidation of soot collected in the particulate filter. This helps regenerate the filter by burning off deposited soot, reducing the risk of clogging and maintaining the filter’s effectiveness over time. By combining nitrogen oxide reduction and particulate removal in a single coated filter, the system achieves compact and efficient exhaust gas purification.

Overall, the approach improves exhaust cleanup by coordinating oxidation, exhaust composition measurement, additive dosing, catalytic nitrogen oxide reduction, and soot filtration. The controlled adjustment of the additive injection according to the nitrogen dioxide-to-nitrogen oxides ratio allows the catalytic process to operate under favorable conditions, while the particulate filter simultaneously captures and oxidizes soot. This integrated method provides an effective way to reduce both nitrogen oxides and particulate emissions from combustion exhaust gas.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract for an exhaust aftertreatment method that oxidizes exhaust components, measures the NO2/NOx ratio, controls additive dosing based on that ratio, and reduces NOx in a catalytically coated particulate filter.
counterfactuals.output: A method for exhaust-gas aftertreatment of an internal combustion engine is disclosed. Exhaust gas containing nitrogen oxides and particulate matter is passed through an oxidation catalyst to oxidize at least one exhaust component, including conversion of NO to NO₂. Downstream of the oxidation catalyst, a NO₂/NOx ratio is determined, directly or indirectly, from sensor signals or a model. An amount of a reducing additive, preferably an ammonia-forming reagent such as urea solution, is metered into the exhaust gas as a function of the determined NO₂/NOx ratio. The exhaust gas and additive are then supplied to a particulate filter having a catalytic coating configured for selective catalytic reduction of NOx. By controlling additive dosing based on the NO₂/NOx ratio, NOx conversion in the coated particulate filter is improved while limiting additive slip and supporting particulate oxidation.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a formal patent claim summary describing a method and system for treating an exhaust stream containing nitrogen oxides using oxidation, determination of a nitrogen dioxide to nitrogen oxides ratio, additive injection, and catalytic filter reduction.
counterfactuals.output:
A method and system are provided for treating an exhaust stream containing nitrogen oxides (NOx). In one aspect, the method comprises passing the exhaust stream through an oxidation catalyst to oxidize at least a portion of nitric oxide (NO) in the exhaust stream to nitrogen dioxide (NO₂), thereby producing an oxidized exhaust stream. A nitrogen dioxide to nitrogen oxides ratio of the oxidized exhaust stream is determined, directly or indirectly, using one or more sensors, estimators, or control algorithms. Based at least in part on the determined ratio, a quantity of a reductant or additive is injected into the oxidized exhaust stream upstream of a catalytic filter. The catalytic filter comprises a filtration substrate carrying a catalytic material effective to reduce nitrogen oxides in the presence of the additive while also removing particulate matter from the exhaust stream. The injected additive is controlled so as to promote selective catalytic reduction of nitrogen oxides across the catalytic filter and to maintain or approach a desired NO₂/NOx ratio for improved reduction efficiency.

In another aspect, the system comprises an exhaust conduit configured to receive an exhaust stream containing nitrogen oxides; an oxidation catalyst disposed in the exhaust conduit and configured to oxidize NO to NO₂; at least one sensor or estimator configured to determine a NO₂/NOx ratio downstream of the oxidation catalyst; an additive injection device positioned downstream of the oxidation catalyst and upstream of a catalytic filter; a controller operatively coupled to the sensor or estimator and to the additive injection device, the controller being configured to regulate an amount of additive injected into the exhaust stream based on the determined NO₂/NOx ratio; and a catalytic filter positioned downstream of the additive injection device, the catalytic filter being configured to filter particulate matter and catalytically reduce nitrogen oxides using the injected additive.

The additive may comprise ammonia, urea, an ammonia precursor, a hydrocarbon, or another reductant suitable for catalytic NOx reduction. The controller may further be configured to adjust injection as a function of one or more operating parameters including exhaust temperature, exhaust mass flow, engine operating condition, NOx concentration, particulate loading, catalyst aging, or desired conversion efficiency. The catalytic filter may include a wall-flow filter substrate coated with a selective catalytic reduction catalyst, and the oxidation catalyst may be a diesel oxidation catalyst positioned upstream of the catalytic filter.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a technical invention disclosure paragraph for a vehicle exhaust treatment system where NOx reduction is performed in a particulate filter with catalytic coating and the reductant supply is controlled according to the NO2/NOx ratio after oxidation.
counterfactuals.output: Disclosed is a vehicle exhaust aftertreatment system and control method in which selective catalytic reduction of nitrogen oxides is integrated with particulate filtration. The system includes, in exhaust-flow order, an oxidation catalyst configured to oxidize at least a portion of NO in the exhaust stream to NO₂, a particulate filter having a catalytic coating effective for NOx reduction in the presence of a reductant, and a reductant dosing device arranged upstream of the catalytically coated particulate filter. A controller determines or estimates an NO₂/NOx ratio downstream of the oxidation catalyst and upstream of the particulate filter, for example using one or more exhaust gas sensors, catalyst temperature data, engine operating parameters, and/or a stored oxidation catalyst model. The controller regulates the amount, timing, or frequency of reductant supply to the particulate filter as a function of the determined NO₂/NOx ratio, such that reductant dosing is increased, decreased, delayed, or inhibited depending on whether the ratio is within a range favorable to fast SCR reactions, standard SCR reactions, or undesired reductant slip and byproduct formation. By adapting reductant supply to the post-oxidation NO₂/NOx ratio, the system improves NOx conversion efficiency within the catalytically coated particulate filter while maintaining particulate filtration capability, reducing ammonia slip, and accommodating changes in exhaust temperature, catalyst aging, soot loading, and engine operating conditions.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: In patent language, describe an exhaust treatment process comprising first oxidation of nitrogen/carbon/hydrogen compounds, calculating the amount ratio of NO2 to total NOx, active dosing of an additive, and catalytic reduction in a soot-oxidizing particulate filter.
counterfactuals.output:
A method for treating an exhaust gas stream from a combustion source, the exhaust gas stream comprising nitrogen compounds, carbon compounds, hydrogen compounds, particulate matter, and nitrogen oxides (NOx), the method comprising:

1. **Oxidizing the exhaust gas stream** in a first oxidation stage by contacting the exhaust gas stream with an oxidation catalyst under conditions effective to oxidize at least a portion of one or more nitrogen-containing, carbon-containing, and hydrogen-containing compounds present in the exhaust gas stream, thereby forming an oxidized exhaust gas stream containing nitric oxide (NO) and nitrogen dioxide (NO₂);

2. **Determining an NO₂/NOx amount ratio** by calculating, measuring, estimating, or otherwise deriving a ratio of an amount of NO₂ to a total amount of NOx in the oxidized exhaust gas stream, wherein the total amount of NOx comprises NO and NO₂;

3. **Actively dosing an additive** into the oxidized exhaust gas stream downstream of the first oxidation stage, wherein an amount of the additive dosed is controlled as a function of the determined NO₂/NOx amount ratio, the additive comprising a reductant or reductant precursor suitable for selective catalytic reduction of NOx; and

4. **Catalytically reducing NOx in a particulate filter** by passing the exhaust gas stream containing the dosed additive through a catalytically active particulate filter configured to trap soot and to promote oxidation of soot retained therein, wherein the catalytically active particulate filter comprises a selective catalytic reduction catalyst effective to reduce at least a portion of the NOx with the additive while simultaneously or intermittently oxidizing particulate matter retained in the filter.

In certain embodiments, the first oxidation stage comprises a diesel oxidation catalyst configured to oxidize hydrocarbons, carbon monoxide, and nitric oxide. The NO₂/NOx amount ratio may be determined using one or more sensors, a stored engine map, a catalyst model, a temperature-dependent conversion model, or combinations thereof. The active dosing of the additive may comprise metering ammonia, urea, an aqueous urea solution, ammonium carbamate, or another ammonia-forming compound into the exhaust gas stream. The dosing rate may be increased, decreased, interrupted, or otherwise modulated in response to the calculated NO₂/NOx amount ratio so as to provide a desired stoichiometric relationship between the additive and NOx entering the particulate filter.

The particulate filter may comprise a wall-flow filter substrate coated or impregnated with a catalyst composition capable of both soot oxidation and selective catalytic reduction. The soot oxidation may be promoted by NO₂ generated in the first oxidation stage, by catalytic material present in or on the filter, or by both. The process thereby provides integrated reduction of NOx and removal of particulate matter from the exhaust gas stream.

counterfactuals.prompt: Create an abstract for an invention related to diesel exhaust purification, including NOx-containing exhaust, upstream oxidation, NO2/NOx ratio determination, controlled additive supply, and reduction in a catalytic particulate filter.
counterfactuals.output: An exhaust purification system and method for treating diesel engine exhaust gas containing nitrogen oxides (NOx) are disclosed. The exhaust gas is subjected to an upstream oxidation treatment to convert at least a portion of nitrogen monoxide (NO) to nitrogen dioxide (NO₂), thereby adjusting the NO₂/NOx ratio of the exhaust stream. The NO₂/NOx ratio is determined directly or indirectly from sensed or modeled operating parameters, and the supply of a reducing additive is controlled as a function of the determined ratio. The additive is introduced into the exhaust gas upstream of a catalytic particulate filter. In the catalytic particulate filter, particulate matter is retained and oxidized, while NOx is reduced in the presence of the additive over a catalytic coating. By coordinating upstream oxidation, NO₂/NOx ratio determination, and controlled additive dosing, the system improves NOx conversion efficiency, promotes particulate filter regeneration, and reduces emissions over varying diesel engine operating conditions.
